title: The Day the Term of a Given-Up Protection Plan Is Counted From
content:
When a Pass and Trip Protection plan is given up, the term whose run is measured is counted from one of three
days.

1. Where the plan's record carries a day cover began and the plan's premium is collected alongside the covered
   holding's instalments, the term is counted from the day cover began.
2. Where the covered holding's record under the Season Pass Programme shows it given up in the season, the
   term is counted from the day the covered holding was given up.
3. In every other case the term is counted from the day the last premium entry was raised on the plan.

**Reading the ladder.** The three are read in the order given. A plan whose premium rides on the covered
holding's instalments and whose record carries a day cover began takes that day, whatever the covered holding
has since done. Only where that first case fails does the covered holding's own standing come into it, and
then the day taken is the day that holding's record shows it was given up. Failing both, the day taken is that
of the most recent premium entry standing on the plan's protection account.

**Illustrations (hypothetical inputs).** A plan riding on the covered holding's instalments, its record
carrying a day cover began: the term is counted from that day. A plan collected in a single payment whose
covered holding's record shows the pass given up in January: the term is counted from that January day. A plan
collected in a single payment whose covered holding still stands: the term is counted from the day the last
premium entry was raised on the plan.
